executive-summary.what: A way to shape data so each important decision can be made from one tiny, aligned, atomic snapshot (capsule)
executive-summary.why: Replace multi-step joins, locks, and partial state with deterministic, nanosecond-class decisions
executive-summary.novelty: Store the decision itself (pre-digested truth), not just raw inputs. Publish whole truth at once; readers see all-old or all-new, never torn.
executive-summary.how: Define capsules (64-1024 bits), assign one writer, publish via two-phase commit (odd to even version). Readers do one load, one branch.
executive-summary.tagline: One word - One read - One decision

target-audience.audience: Solo builders who want speed + reliability without a giant framework
Teams that need predictable tail latency (p99/p999) and auditability
Projects that must degrade, not die under stress (network spikes, bursts, news)

glossary.term: A tiny, aligned, fixed-size snapshot that contains enough truth to decide immediately
Single-Writer, Many-Readers ownership; the writer publishes snapshots; readers never lock
The writer marks a snapshot valid by toggling a small header (odd to even version or commit=1)
Readers load a capsule (often a single cache line) with one atomic read instruction
Quality levels L0 to L3 controlled by a tiny breaker capsule

design-rules.rule: Shape the data to the decision. Pack only what a reader needs to branch now.
One writer, many readers. If multiple sources feed a capsule, add an aggregator writer.
Publish in two phases. Build payload - set ver odd - write tail - flip header (ver even or commit=1).
Single cache line where possible. 64-512 bits are ideal; 1024 bits for portfolio/time tables.
Fixed-point over floats. Ticks, basis points, milliseconds - tiny integers, no FP stalls.
No locks in the hot path. Readers do load(Relaxed); use Acquire only if you dereference a freshly published pointer.
Degrade, don't die. A tiny breaker capsule (L0..L3) controls quality globally.
Always log. A 16-byte hash-chained ledger entry on every important event.

fractal-principle.description: Repeat the same rule at every scale

applications.level: One capsule ranks where to add/cut risk
One tile (1 kB) snapshots counters and last hashes for crash-safe recovery

fractal-principle.insight: The same SWeMR + commit rule applies at each level. It scales because the rule never changes.

publish-protocol.step: Set ver ODD; fill payload; compute checksum; set ver_tail=ver
Release-store head with commit=1, ver++ (EVEN), stale=0
Optional: set stale=1 to cancel/replace quickly

reader-accept-rule.step: Load head (Relaxed). Accept if commit=1, ver EVEN; verify ver == ver_tail
Do one branch to decide; Acquire only if following a pointer

swemr-pattern.read-operation: Readers load capsule with atomic load, no locks
swemr-pattern.write-operation: Writer builds payload, commits with Release store

commit-flip.odd-version: Build payload, payload not yet committed
commit-flip.even-version: Readers can safely use the data

swemr-pattern.acquire-usage: Use Acquire ordering ONLY if following a freshly published pointer

pattern.name: Circuit Breaker
pattern.purpose: Fast fail coordination with quality levels
pattern.fields: state/level + cause bits (L0 normal ... L3 pause)

pattern.name: Cost/Edge Gate
pattern.fields: gross, fees, slip, net, min threshold
pattern.decision: One read yes/no: net greater than or equal to min?

pattern.name: Risk Envelope
pattern.purpose: Risk gates for prop rules and quotas

pattern.name: Execution Bundle
pattern.purpose: Complete execution specification in one publish

pattern.name: Latency Ticket
pattern.fields: f2d, d2a, a2f, jitter, loss, qpos

pattern.name: DOM Slice
pattern.fields: L1-L5 bid/ask for two instruments + derived metrics

pattern.name: Event Lockout
pattern.decision: Whether trading is restricted by events

breaker-pattern.reader-behavior: Apply L rules instantly (size multipliers, route restrictions)
breaker-pattern.writer-behavior: Decide when to raise/lower based on thresholds + dwell times

alignment-types.code: #[repr(C, align(64))] pub struct Aeb512 { pub w0: core::sync::atomic::AtomicU128, pub w1: core::sync::atomic::AtomicU128, pub w2: core::sync::atomic::AtomicU128, pub w3: core::sync::atomic::AtomicU128, }

fixed-point-helpers.rule: Keep conversions centralized; never scatter FP math in readers

new-capsule-checklist.step: Define the decision the reader must make in one branch
List fields that are strictly necessary (scores, timers, caps)
Pick size (64-512 bits usually) and fixed-point units
Choose the single writer and update cadence
Design head/tail with ver (odd to even), optional checksum16
Add unit, property, stress, bench tests
Log ALE-128 on every publish/consume decision

testing-plan.tier: Bit packing, range limits, fixed-point conversions
Never accept odd ver, head==tail or reject, hysteresis/dwell never chatter
Concurrent writers (via aggregator), reader flood, clock skew
Feed recorded inputs; reader decisions must be identical
Per-read 5-20 ns or less; publish 50-400 ns or less depending on size

component.name: Ledger Line
component.description: Every important event produces 16 bytes with a hash link

component.name: Epoch Tile
component.recovery: On startup, scan for last valid tile and resume

capability.name: Deterministic tail
capability.description: Decisions are constant time, so p99 approximately equals median

capability.name: Hot swapping policy
capability.description: Push a new RLT and the whole system's behavior changes without code edits

capability.name: Instant global reactions
capability.description: A tiny breaker flip synchronizes quality across modules in nanoseconds

capability.name: Audit you can prove
capability.description: Hash-chained ledger + tile digests give forensic-grade trails

capability.name: Fractal portability
capability.description: The same capsule rules work on a laptop UI, an exchange router, or a robot loop

migration-guide.step: Pick one decision that currently stalls/recomputes often
Draft a capsule that answers it directly (64-128 bits)
Wrap the old code behind the capsule writer; stop recomputing in the reader
Gate the reader to only use the capsule
Add breaker and ledger; measure tail latency before/after

security.rule: Keep capsule packers/commit logic in a private crate
Never expose raw capsules over external APIs; export summarized, human fields only
Watermark builds; log policy_id, node_id, and last hashes in ET tiles

fill-in-template.field: [Describe in one sentence what the reader must decide]
[what readers do on green / amber / red]

architecture-flow.description: Read path: ~4 capsule reads - 1 publish. Publishers do the heavy lifting off-path and commit whole truths atomically.

closing.philosophy: Choose the decision, shape one tiny truth, publish once, and let everything else move at cache-line speed.
closing.result: A system that is fast, steady, and easy to reason about - and small enough for a solo builder to own end-to-end.
